findings.summary: Swapping the first boundary word for a fixed phrase doubles articles.
findings.evidence: The steward and Hestia most often write the first list word after an article ("the <word> approves", "an <word>"). A fixed swap to 'the person running Athena' gives "the the person running Athena" or "an the person running Athena". Neither the helper's unit tests nor the per-writer tests check this. Fix: When a rewritten word follows 'the', 'a' or 'an' (any case), take the article into the replacement too, so 'The <word>' becomes 'The person running Athena'. Add a unit test for the article forms and for the possessive.
findings.location: Plan step 1 / Decision 1 (replacement table for the first boundary word)

findings.summary: Replacing only the matched fragment leaves broken paths.
findings.evidence: boundary_fragments() in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs:538-550 holds path pieces such as the root-dot prefix and the home-user prefix. These match anywhere in a line. Replacing only the matched fragment inside a longer path leaves a broken path made of the placeholder plus the rest of the original path. Fix: Replace the whole whitespace-delimited token that holds a fragment with the placeholder (for example '[local path]'), and add a unit test with a full machine path.
findings.location: Plan step 1 (fragment placeholder) and Open question 3

findings.summary: Silent rewrites inside quoted file and commit content make the quotes inaccurate, and the claim about the failure's real source is unverified.
findings.evidence: In work_decisions.rs:198-246, path_text and commit_text copy file and commit text verbatim inside fences, so the request presents it as an exact quote. A silent rewrite inside a quoted code file (an identifier, for example) misquotes the file to the reader and producer. The plan also says the cited content is the 'real source' of the 2026-10-29 failure, but the request describes the word as being in the proposal's own description. The snapshot has no records to settle which is right. Fix: When approve_request rewrote anything, add one line to the request saying that boundary words in the copied content were reworded, so quotes are not taken as exact. Describe the cited-content cause as a second path, not as the confirmed cause.
findings.location: Decision 3 / step 5 (approve_request cleans copied file, job and commit content)

findings.summary: The approve-work test does not seed the word in the stored work item's title, which is the reported case.
findings.evidence: The approve-work test seeds the boundary word only in the cited source content. The request's own case is a proposal whose description (the work item title, which approve_request copies in as item.title at line 280) carried the word, including items already stored before this fix. Fix: Also put a fragment-built boundary word in the committed work item's title. Assert that approve_work succeeds and the stored request is clean, so the stored-title path is shown as well.

findings.summary: The extra helper call in try_error_review repeats the cleaning that StewardRequest::new already does.
findings.evidence: try_error_review (hestia.rs:1747) builds its text only through root_cause_request, which calls StewardRequest::new (hestia.rs:370). Once StewardRequest::new cleans its input, the extra helper calls in hestia.rs are redundant. Tests (b) and (c) also exercise the same builder. Fix: Keep a single visible call in root_cause_request_at to meet criterion 5. Drop the duplicate call in try_error_review, or say why it is needed.

summary: I read the code the plan names and checked it. All of it exists: boundary_words, boundary_fragments and boundary_scan in briefs.rs; StewardRequest::new, validate_item, check_key, blind_spot_change, decide and RequestQueue in steward.rs; root_cause_request_at, try_error_review and error_review in hestia.rs; apply_answer and redact_all in introspect.rs; approve_request and approve_work in work_decisions.rs; refuse_banned_input and scan_request_input in reading.rs; and make_athena in test_support.rs. The plan fixes the fault in two places. All steward-channel requests are built in StewardRequest::new, so cleaning there covers the steward, Hestia and the other builders. Approve-work's own request is built in approve_request, which copies in the stored title and cited content, so cleaning there covers old stored items. The helper sits next to the scan it must match and re-runs the scan, so it cannot hand back text that still fails. Each demonstration calls a production function through an existing seam and would fail without the cleaning. Test (b) also fails at queue's admission scan, and the approve-work test fails at ask. The only test double is a canned reader, and the code under test is production code. No athena.toml field is added, and the work fits one producer run. The soundness problems are minor: the fixed phrase swap reads badly after an article ('the the person running Athena'), a fragment swap can leave broken paths, rewriting quoted file content should be flagged in the request, and the approve-work test should also seed the word in the stored title. None of these leaves a criterion unshown, so the verdict is accept.
